info.title: FitnessClub REST API
info.summary: Workout, nutrition, health, coaching and billing for the FitnessClub plugin.
info.description:
This document is **generated from the live route registry**, not written by hand —
every type, enum, bound and required flag below came from the schema the request
validator actually enforces.

## Authentication

The plugin owns its accounts. A WordPress login is not a FitnessClub login, and a
WordPress administrator with no FitnessClub account is anonymous to this API.

Two things authenticate a request, and the front end receives both in its boot
payload:

- the session **cookie**, sent automatically for same-origin requests;
- the **`X-FC-CSRF`** header, required on every method except GET, HEAD
  and OPTIONS.

The CSRF token is bound to the session and expires with it, so there is no refresh
step: a rejected token means the session is gone and the correct response is to
show the sign-in screen.

## Errors

Every failure is a WordPress `WP_Error` envelope with a stable, namespaced code.
**Branch on `code`, never on `message`** — messages are translated and may change.

## Pagination

Every list endpoint takes `page` and `per_page` (default 20, maximum 100) and
returns `X-WP-Total` and `X-WP-TotalPages` headers.

## Response bodies

Request schemas are exact, because they are generated. **Response schemas are
modelled only where the shape is contract-critical** — the boot payload and the
error envelope. Everywhere else a response is described as a generic object rather
than being guessed at; an inaccurate schema is worse than an absent one.

**Public.** Refused *with* a session, so a call made while signed in cannot silently swap accounts.

post.summary: Sign in as an external client
post.description:
For **mobile apps and third-party clients only**. A browser should use `/auth/login`: it already holds a cookie, and a bearer token in JavaScript is one any XSS can exfiltrate and — unlike a cookie — cannot be cleared. Returns a **15-minute** access token plus a long-lived refresh token; nothing here sets a cookie.

Off by default. A site that has not enabled it answers **404**, and one that enabled it without configuring a signing secret answers **503** — different problems with different fixes.

**Public.** Refused *with* a session, so a call made while signed in cannot silently swap accounts.

200.description: An access/refresh pair and the account it belongs to.

post.summary: Exchange a refresh token for a new pair
post.description:
**The refresh token is rotated on every use** and the old one is revoked immediately — so store the new one. That is what makes a stolen refresh token detectable rather than permanent: the thief and the real client race, and whichever presents the stale token second is refused, surfacing the theft as a sign-out instead of a silent parallel session.

**Public.** No session required.

200.description: A new access/refresh pair. The presented refresh token is now dead.

429.description: Rate limited. `retry_after` and the `Retry-After` header say how long to wait.

post.description:
Takes the refresh token in the body rather than acting on the caller's access token, so a client can revoke a grant it is not currently using — which is what "sign out this device" needs. **Always answers 200**, whether or not the token existed: reporting that would make this an oracle for guessing tokens.

The access token stays cryptographically valid until it expires, but every request re-checks that the grant behind it is live, so it stops working at once.

**Public.** No session required.

post.description:

**Requires a signed-in member.**

sessionCookie.name: fc_session_*
sessionCookie.description: The FitnessClub session cookie, set on sign-in. Sent automatically for same-origin requests.

csrfToken.name: X-FC-CSRF
csrfToken.description: Required on every method except GET, HEAD and OPTIONS. Delivered in the boot payload as `csrf`.

message.description: Human-readable and translated. Never branch on this.

Boot.description: Everything a front end needs for its first frame. Delivered two ways: as the `data-boot` attribute on `#fc-app` in the rendered shell, and as the body of `GET /auth/me` (which omits the transport-only keys `restUrl`, `csrf`, `brand`, `locale` and `flags`). Login and register return the full object, so signing in needs no second request.

user.description: Null when nobody is signed in.

subscriptions.description: A member holds one subscription per trainer, plus the platform tier.

trainers.description: The member's coaches. A member may have several.

entitlements.description: Merged across every active subscription: booleans union, caps take the maximum (never the sum), null beats any number.

theme.description: Colour, typography and layout tokens, also emitted as `--fc-*` custom properties on `#fc-app`. A front-end theme may use them or ignore them.

base.description: The configurable front-end slug. Never hardcode it.

spa.description: Which app the server resolved for this role.

restUrl.description: Shell only. REST root for this site.

csrf.description: Shell only. Send as `X-FC-CSRF` on every non-GET.

brand.description: Shell only. The configured brand name.
